review_text: Very good professor, excels at explaining the concepts to students in basic terms and drawing insights from industry standards. Friendly and approachable.

His lectures are hard to listen to. Homework is easy but tests are horrible. They are also the main graded segments. Handwriting is legible but hard to read. Claims his class is easy because the topics are easy but does not teach as such. grades very lightly. I messed up on my midterm but he bumped it up a few. i dont feel like i learned. :[

Lectures are nothing more than reading slides (which are already awful and made by a different professor 5+ years ago) and his voice is so quiet that students have to ask him to speak up every class. Final was 30% of final grade, bloated with more questions so it's actually worth more than 30% in the end. SFSU Machine Structures is a scam course.

He's the only professor (not a lecturer) currently teaching CSC 220. An extremely experienced programmer, he incorporates plenty of live coding into his lectures, making it an excellent way to learn Java programming and data structures. He is vary caring and easy going. I highly recommend taking CSC 220 with him.

I believe 95% of the kids get either A/B in the course. Attendance quizzes, 6 homework assignments and a midterm and final are the majority of this class. If you have quarter of a brain you'll do fine.

mandatory lecture quizzes that you work on by urself then he shows how to solve.20% of grade. HW not long, 40% of grade. 2 Multiple choice exams 20% each. can explain anything. He is worth being your first option for professor. Low stress, good for people working or have other obligations in life

Good teacher! took him for 220, is very passionate about the subject and helps explain, has quizzes every class but don't worry he goes over it so its impossible to not get full points, homework assignments are easy to understand, midterms are based off quizzes he give during class. 10/10 professor would 100% take him again

Professor Akila fostered an environment where critical thinking and deeper understanding were valued. Challenging topics like recursion, linked lists, and trees were broken down into clear, digestible explanations with practical examples that connected theory to real-world applications.
One of the best professors I ever had.

Very good class, learned a lot and it's very easy to get a good grade if you lock in and participate in the lectures. Final/Midterm is multiple choice, making it so much better in comparison to the written CS tests, which made me understand the topics much better as I was able to focus rather than worry about the actual written code. GOATED
Took him for CSC 220, Data Structures. The old adage rings true, "those who can't do, teach." Avoid this professor at all costs.
great

I recently took CSC 665 with Professor Akila de Silva. He is not a tough grader. The course consist of assignments and quizzes making up 60% of the overall grade, followed by two midterms, each worth 10%, and a final exam worth 20%. Also, there was an optional mini-project that offered 10% extra credit, which was a great opportunity for students.

Took CS620 with this professor. I found the environment difficult for asking questions. When students sought clarification, she often responded with laughter rather than an explanation, which discouraged class participation. I'd recommend looking for a section that better fosters open discussion.

Takes things too personally, lacks professionalism. Teaches some concepts well and most concepts horribly. Outdated teaching practices. Hate the way she pronounces "matrices". Lecture slides are a mess, and she goes through them so fast. I uploaded all the slides onto ChatGPT to learn the material. Also, HW is irrelevant and not discussed at all.

Very difficult class as the lectures were not very helpful in the quizzes nor homework, and you are expected to learn on your own for most of the homework assignments. Her slides for class are also very confusing to look at (jumbled up, especially if you are trying to look at it before a quiz) and explanations are confusing as well.

Very impressive for a week and a half, then disappointments and more disappointments. She is very unorganized and apparently unprepared for the class. However, she preaches and blames it all on students. Her knowledge is very outdated. She is too busy with so many roles and offices she is holding. No time for teaching or students. Grading is awful.

A drama queen. She tries hard to be young and sweet. Her lectures are confusing. She tests on things she does not cover. Her assignments are totally outdated and irrelevant in some ways. It is to tell that she does not prepare for her lectures. She reads of the ppt slides and often loses track of what she is saying.

if you aren't good with attendance and showing up on time, don't sign up for this class. attendance, 12 weekly quizzes that are based on lectures, and 6 homework assignments are 90% of the class. The quizzes are somewhat tough but if you read the lectures you should be fine. The homework assignments are vague, so ask questions if you're confused.

She is very sweet and wants everyone to learn and succeed in the class, however, her lectures are not engaging; she reads from the slides and her explanations are vague.Quizes are kind of hard but if you learn the material you should do ok. Homework is outdated and sometimes difficult to understand so you do not really know what to do.

Easily one of the best professors. Her lectures are amazing and funnily enough, NLP is probably the best "intro to AI" course simply because she explains all the concepts so well. Attendance is mandatory and there are weekly quizzes based off the slides from the previous week. Do the work, attend class, and it's an easy A and you'll learn lots.
Professor Kulkarni is not a good pick for this class, unfortunately she is the only professor who teaches NLP at SFSU. I would rather take an online course from Coursera.
Very interesting lectures with a caring and respectful professor. Fun assignments but sometimes are a bit tedious due to some outdated packages to install and fix.

She gives out homework assignments about once a week but most of them are manageable. She does offer extensions from time to time as well. She sets up the grading so that each assignment is worth about 2.5% of your grade so if you don't do well on some assignments you can still do well in the course. There's also a final paper but it's very simple.
Great professor. She knows what she is doing and is patient. If you don't show up and don't do the work you won't pass.

First day. She was a gem. But then her TA came. TOTALLY hard to understand. Goes way too fast. If she makes her group involvement portion worth 40%, where all of it is based on how we learn from him, I would not suggest taking this course.

I don't get why people give her a bad rep. She was chill and nice professor. Always tried her best to answer question. Yes there were a bit of work for the total grade, but 1/3 of it was like free points?? And the midterm she let us retake it for a better grade. She tries to help you to save money by finding a free pdf version of the book.
Her grade isn't based on how well you perform, there are so many other factors are inappropriate to mention here. DO NOT take her class if you can. Worst professor in my student career ever!
Lectures are in order and neat homework assignment. Requires coding skills or opportunity to improve it. Expects committed students and no leniency.
I felt like I learned a lot in her class. If you read the book, and do the work you will probably pass. She is very nice and will listen if you have a legitimate problem.

Dr. Anagha Kulkarni is probably one of the worst teachers I've had here at SFSU. She's bad at explaining, her powerpoint notes are not helpful at all. If you have no prior background in programming this class will be hard. I basically had to teach my self. I advise not to take her!

Kulkarni's overall method for the class works for me. You have 4 homeworks that get you using SQLite, then 6 Quizzes that cover 1 chapter each and the Final which is comprehensive. There was 2 extra credits worth 1 Homework each, basically you had 2 free quizzes. Homework and Quizzes don't overlap, and having the occasional quiz forced studying.
She is explaining very well. Only you have to show up, ask her. The tests are not that hard. She goes through examples prior the tests and you would see same examples in your test.

Kulkarni is a good professor that wants her students too succeed. This class consist of 5 quizzes, 1 midterm, and 1 final. All test are doable if you study beforehand. You work with the SQL language to modify database tables. There are some concepts that are hard to get used too at first, such as index trees and JDBC, but become clear afterwards
Tough teacher. Would not recommend. There are better professors to choose from. Work your schedule around and avoid this teacher!

If you dont have any foundaton for cs, this class will definitely help you a lot, but first, you have to be a indepentdent student, and you have to know how to learn things. This class will teach you how to learn cs, and you will be very good at it if you do all the exercise that the professor assign to you. Thats my experience.

Take her if you already know ProgrammingJava. I took her the second time and most of the work was really time consuming. If you don't, you'll have a harder time with her assignments and will get very little help. I don't recommens this professor.

She expects you to have a CS background, but it's an INTRO class. She's condescending to students and makes them feel stupid if they ask a question. She was grading the entire class based on the students who had prior CS experience, which is unfair to those who didn't. Me and a bunch of students ended up withdrawing. DON'T TAKE HER.

Her powerpoints are helpful but her tests can be tricky. She doesn't give any study guides so be prepared to study through all the powerpoints. The final was tricky but was mostly non-cummulative though she said everything is cummulative. I advise not to take her!

After the last HW we got assigned, I agree with the last poster. She needs to do a better job with the HW. And she really doesn't bother responding to emails. Really shows how uninterested she is in teaching a Intro Class.

Does not explain things very well. Gives incredibly hard homework that covers material that we have not gone over in class. Does not explain things clearly and gets mad when you don't understand something that she thinks is simple. Wastes time calling out kids in class. Would not recommend

She assumes you have a background in programming and doesn't really explain ANYTHING! I am not a csc major nor have I ever taken any programming course before this and I struggled a lot. She's not clear, doesn't teach anything and her accent is horrible. Don't take her if you're new to csc!! She's a nice person but you're pretty much teaching yourself. Avoid her unless you actually know programming.

Every class she was condescending toward students. She actually insulted us for having questions and not knowing the answer before asking them. She's not helpful. You pretty much are self teaching yourself CS with an angry boss over your shoulder making sure you follow pedantic rules. She obviously doesn't want to be teaching such a basic class.

This class is pretty chill I give her that. But her homework needs to be explained better. It is very confusing which makes it time consuming. Her midterm was hard and unfair because it was the only midterm we had in this class. Literally just memorize her powerpoint slides and you'll get at least a B or B- in her class.Make sure you get A's on HW.

Great teacher. Really a chill class, but be sure you do the work and practice. Her powerpoint slides are really helpful. She will help if you have questions. I like that she wants us to do in-class exercises to help us get the hang of Programming. She really cares for her students. I recommend her if you're a beginner.

She is really chill and makes sure all students understand the material. Her quizzes are easy, and her tests are not that bad. If you go to the class daily and review the materials, you will get an A. She is also really helpful during office hours. You don't need the book, everything is found in the power points. Take her!! I was never stressed..

A new teacher at SFSU from CMU. She is lenient and extremely helpful if you go to office hours(as are most Professors). As a new teacher you can tell that she really cares that her students learn the material.
One of the most easy going professors at SFSU. You'll have fun learning from him if you are really interested in learning the art of Full stack development.
One of the best teachers I've had so far at SFSU. Highly recommend. Industry experience and wants students to succeed.

Professor Scott is one of the best computer science teachers I have ever had. His projects are straightforward and you will learn new things. Even when they get difficult, the solutions give you the necessary experience for software development projects. He is also accessible outside of class and very helpful.

Professor is very understanding and wants you to succeed. His class is straightforward and you just need to stay up with the work because doing projects last minute is almost a death sentence for your grade. I would recommend, if possible, to do the group projects with people you are familiar with and/or have good work ethic/ communication.

He's an excellent teacher, addressing all questions seriously. One semester entails three solo assignments and a group report, split into three parts. If your group remains active, it's not challenging. Earning points is straightforward, and extra credit is available. Achieving an A shouldn't be too difficult.
Extremely unreasonable grading
Best guy this side of the golden gate bridge

Prof Souza is amazing. I was terrified to take CSC and had a lot of preconceived notions about taking CSC, but all of those fears were shattered by how great a Prof he is. Every topic was presented in an understandable and digestible way. He treats every student with respect and truly wants to see you succeed. Def take his class.

Great professor. Took it in summer, lectures mainly focused on assignments and had recordings. Get ready to read, instructions of assignments are very long but not difficult. Always turned the lecture before assignment deadline into an optional lab session. Attendance as EC and also provided EC on assignments.
He is chill and understanding. His lectures are amazing. He makes us understand the materials easily. Take his class, you will not regret.

Don't take him unless you're unemployed and/or enrolled part-tine. That is where all his good reviews come from. Assignments have prompts up to 20 pages long, or more. And he doesn't prepare you for them at all. Allergic to teaching. Expects students to learn everything on their own. Does not approve W's or pass/no-pass. Hates his job and students.

This course is more about how much you put in. The class lectures were middle of the ground, most of the time it feels like hes just trying to take up time till he hits the end of class. Yeah its a easy course basically a free A. If you do everything and dont use AI you learn quite a bit, but can't say its due to him more so due to the projects.

Took his class over the summer, so it was a bit more accelerated, but the way he taught the material was good and I enjoyed his class overall. It was a solo project which I heard has been turned into a group project, so it was a bit more difficult but he was pretty lenient with the grading.

I don't understand his high rating. He gets very off-topic. I had to watch recordings of lectures even though I attended them. Applying the lectures to the homework is like searching for a needle in a haystack he is so off-topic. Also, I had a very serious injury preventing me from taking the final. He ghosted and failed me like a coward. Unreal!!!
Loved his csc101, felt like rather than straight up zombie coding I was actually learning something, it felt good and he was always there to answer questions.
Good Professor
Best cs teacher ever

The only reason I got through are because of the DL small work groups, being talked to for an hour without being able to do hands on work was just not a good way for myself to be introduced to computer science.
There is not much else to say but he's a good professor
Overall great professor. Graded mainly on three assignments and the final one is a bit tricky, but he gives lots of help in lectures and curves at the end.
Amazing professor.
Professor Souza is the best teacher at SFSU in my opinion. He knows the material and how to teach. Attendance isn't required, but make sure to go to class, or you'll fall behind.
He is alright.
He is the greatest teacher in the world.
overall caring person. has to be one of the top professors at SFSU. thanks for a great semester .

spent the semester working on a project and it was pretty fun but got a little too hand-holdy near the end, quizzes weren't too bad with 2-3 attempts, due dates were fairly flexible with various extensions provided

There are 3 assignments-Calculator, Interpreter, Tank Game(final+presentation).The assignments are difficult but he gives partial credit and extends by a few days.Many people are worried about the tank game but he provides starter code. Also for the presentation some people presented broken code so there isn't anything to worry about :) (fall 2022)

Professor Souza is the best teacher I have ever had, he cares a lot about students and helps a lot with assignments and even with the final project he will guide you through it. He knows a lot about coding and explains the topics very well.

Professor Souza will go out of his way to help you get your quizzes and assignments turned in on time. We have a term project and he helps you a LOT throughout. Attendance is not mandatory as he records each lecture and posts it on canvas.
Professor souza is knowledgable and cares about his students

He basically holds your hand during the semester. Always there for support & extensions if someone needs it. I really appreciate the fact that he uploads his lectures (especially with covid/monkeypox cases on the rise). The way he uses Discord for participation is clever and convenient! Do the Milestones on time & the project will be less stressful

This man is an absolute gem. Makes it very clear what he expects of you in for each and every assignment with quizzes that relate directly back to the slides and lectures videos that he makes available. Is somewhat lecture heavy but thats standard for CS classes in the semester system. (He was my professor him for CSC 413 as well.)

Chill dude. He's kind, caring, extends most of his assignment's deadline by a few days. But DON'T start on your HWs super close to the deadline or else you're gonna have a bad time. Most of them are decently challenging, but not as difficult as other CSC413 classes. Quality > Quantity class in terms of workload. The Tank Game project was fun to do.

I've been taking all classes taught by Souza; incredibly caring, understanding and straight forward in the class. Most of the deadlines he extends a couple of days. Don't slack off, and put effort into it; it's not hard to get an A if you start early, and understand the materials. Recommend buying Jon Duckett books; its good for this class.

Professor Souza created probably one of the best online formats for the pandemic so far. The asynchronistic nature of his lecture set up means its entirely on you to figure out how you want to approach the class, however going through each video one by one you'll have a great understanding on how to tackle the projects given.
I would just say the best Professor I have ever had Very helpful in you r hard times Very understandable I wish he teaches all cs classes I would always take him

Ramps up heavily near the end of the semester, don't procrastinate. Do the readings as soon as you can and really try to understand the subject. Build little projects. For the final project you can complete it using the lecture alone but it will be time consuming. You can also complete the final project using your own research in a faster manner.

His quizzes are fairly easy as long as you do the readings. The assignments however, I would say they're quite difficult since I'm not really good with programming. If you at least put in the effort in his class and asks questions, you will definitely pass. Don't start your assignment at the last minute though, or else you will regret it.

Definitely enjoy his 413 a lot more during summer 2021 time. Anthony himself was the best teacher aside from 2 of my other professors whom I previously had. Would highly recommend those that want to know CSC 317 and 413 to take his class. summertime is the best time. Wish he teaches CSC 415 OS class.

By far one of my favorite professors at SFSU. He makes it very clear to his students what he expects from them and there are never any surprises. He is a fair grader and does a good job at explaining what we need work on. I took him over the summer and I was able to learn a lot in such a short period of time.
Clearly outlines what he wants for the assignments. Provides a lot of resources so that you can complete all of your assignments with A's.

Best professor hands down! really caring for students and highly knowledgeable. makes class fun and enjoyable where students can learn, office hours are tremendously helpful. 4 assignments and easy quizzes with one final project which is covered in extreme detail and FUN. Would definitely take again!
One of my favorite professors. Super chill about deadlines, just put in some effort and he will pass you
The most patient and organized professor. He is a real gem.
Intro to web dev based on 4 assignments, quizzes, and one project. Quizzes can be retaken. Very helpful in office hours.

One of my most favorite professors ever. Anthony really cares for his students. He extended the deadline for the final project twice so students would have the time to catch up and get a good grade. I wish he taught upper division courses :( Would definitely take him again if I could. Highly recommended!

Incredible man. Class was asynchronous, posted videos and slides in a timely matter. Class was pretty straight forward. Had 8 quizzes based on material in videos and slides. He explained homework assignments very detailed, which helped a lot. Definitely recommend <3

Has weekly quizzes based on lectures. Has three assignments, one for HTML, one for CSS, and one for javascript, which all lead up to a term project. He gives you a month to do the term project and helps you do a lot of it in a way where it's manageable and you're able to learn a lot. He's also very accessible through email, discord, and slack!

If you are a beginner on web development, take this class. He is really good with his lectures. His notes are straightforward and match the quizzes really well. His assignments are great. He guides you step by step on how to do them. Web development has so much interesting material. I wish they could expanding the knowledge of JavaScript.

Professor haas experience in the industry which is always nice. The video lectures are straightforward and incredibly useful. Class gets fairly hard by assignment 4. The final project is pretty involved, make sure you give yourself time to work on it. Focus on quality in the first 3 assignments and final becomes way easier.

Good professor. He is an easy grader and as long as you try in the class, you won't fail. All the quizzes were fairly easy if you do the reading. The final wasn't too hard either since some of the questions come from past quizzes. Been taking him for 317, 413, and 415!

Very knowledgeable with the material. Lectures were informative and assigns a project to see what you have learned. Has office to help anybody who has trouble with starting the project. Everything in the final is covered in the lect. Pay attention to his lectures, make sure you know his grading criteria, and ask him question during his office hours

He is absolutely the best professor at SFSU. He use to be student and he knows the real game. He give you assignments that you can actually have ability to do it not some random things to make you fail. He understands the struggles he is not there to make you fail the class. I have been taking him for 317, 413, 415 he is amazing. take it !

Souza was an excellent professor and I really enjoyed his teaching style. As a result of COVID, we switched to per-recorded (live coding) lectures which made it easy to follow the class. Quizes were based heavily on the slides, make sure to study them. If you're serious about programming, this class will be a breeze. Would 100% take him again.
He is really caring and makes you work hard! Go to his office hours and start his projects early and you will pass!
Just gotta say I had a hard time because he's too chill and I'm not that productive while on quarantine. I smashed final project within one month, it was stupid idea but he was nice.

Professor was great at teaching and he was pretty straight forward with what he expected. His quizzes were easy if you reviewed his slides. The final project was creating an easy website (backend and frontend) using html,css, & js. No tests.

You pretty much need to teach yourself entire web dev course. He lectures from slide decks of like 75+ slides then just throws you into the deep end for the final project (making an imgur ish website) so pick a smart partner! I thought I was gonna fail because I had a hard time initially with git, but ended up rounding me from a D+ to a C. Nice guy
He is one of the best CS teachers at SFSU. He is very nice and caring. I have learned a lot from his class. I wish I could take him more. Take him 100% you will not regret.

Intro Web & Software Development. Class consists of him lecturing off PDF slides. I find it hard to learn since he mostly lectures and I learn best from practice/doing. This class requires a lot of self-teaching. He is a very chill and nice grader but I wish he did more examples. Regardless, I would take Souza again in the future

Souza makes the the concepts very easy and understandable. There are 5 projects which are somewhat difficult but manageable, 5 quizzes which isn't bad, and the final is literally combined quizzes. Take him if you can.
Super nice person. Maybe too nice.

Souza is an SFSU student turned professor so he really gets what it's like being a student there. He is super generous when it comes to adding students if there's space. He posts slides online and accessible via the SFSU CS Slack channel. Grade is 4 quizzes (in lieu of midterm), 6 projects, final, and Slack participation.

3 medium difficulty take home labs, 1 difficult term project - create 2 games + presentation, and 1 easy final. This is a class where you are on your own, with not enough resources provided to succeed, most people ended up getting "outside" resources to complete the term project. be good at java and meet the project requirements and you will pass.

I found it helpful when we would program data structures piece by piece as a class. He has a lot of patience for questions. If someone or a group got stuck on a concept he worked with them until they understood. Handwriting code for tests was interesting. A fair grader. Never got to the extra credit but the opportunity was always there.

He's a pretty good teacher. The homework is not very difficult and can be completed if you understand the concepts in the slides. The textbook is not necessary to get a good grade. It's hard to not get an A if you do every assignment.
One of the best professors I have taken at SFSU. If he is available , highly recommend. Actually cares if you put the time and effort into the class and the assignments are very straight forward.

Souza has always been a pretty good teacher. His lectures are a little hard to follow sometimes but overall not that bad. His grading criteria is really simple and gives lots of opportunities for extra credit. His tests are pretty straightforward. 10/10 IGN review

Great teacher, very helpful. Attendance is optional, though encouraged with extra credit, but if you already know programming (like myself) you can not attend any class the entire semester and still get over 100% final grade. 1 midterm and 1 final, plus an online project about once a week or ever other week.

Definitely take him if you can. He's always happy to help and offers a bunch of extra credit. Attendance isn't mandatory and he answers emails quickly. If not a lot of people turned in the homework, he would often extend the deadline. Overall a great teacher !

Great teacher and very helpful. Especially because he understands the perspective of the students unlike many professors who are living in a fantasy land where we are all only taking 1 class. This is a lab so you must show up and do each lab. If you do, it is an easy class to pass.

Great, laid back professor who made class fun. It's an easy A as long as you show up to class to complete lab worksheets, and play with practice examples before implementing them on your website. At the end, you have to present your website you've been working on all semester. We learned a lot of web-based languages, and he was very helpful in OH.

Great professor. He's more than willing to help in and out of class. Overall, a laid back grad student who can easily relate to his students. It was a fun lab, learning a ton of new languages used in web development. Show up, do the lab worksheets, you will pass.

Very nice professor and a very fun class where you build a website from scratch using languages such as Linux, Unix, JavaScript, Bootstrap, Python, LAMP, etc every class. Laid back and willing to help if you're stuck on anything. Make sure you show up and do the work and play with practice examples before implementing them. Highly recommended.

Good class. Teacher is a grad student, laid back but clear. You get what you put into the class, as you'll be exposed to a number of languages and tools used primarily in web development. You get just a taste, as every lab covers something different. Some examples: HTML, CSS, Javascript, jQuery, Python, LAMP (Linux, Apache, MySQL, PHP).

I had him for an 8am class, he is helpful but i didn't like his teaching style. I felt as if he lectured too much and didn't give a lot of in class practice. To pass, you would need to go to his office hours.
He is nice guy always happy to help!

Souza is a graduate student pretty much there just to make sure you do what youre suppose too. This class was fun and interesting since you get to make a website from scratch for your portfolio. At the end you have to present the website you been working on all semester to get credit for the class.
He will wear a giants cap almost every day. He is a graduate student with a wicked beard and he is an awesome guy. His exams are easy as long as you do the work and he gives lots of extra credit!!!

He had absolutely no energy in any of his lessons it was very dry. If you don't have any previous CAD experience this class may be tough. He is rigorous on how you draft and present drawings, grades very harshly. I will give him the benefit of the doubt because it was an evening class, everyone wants to go home. He's a mediocre Professor.

Down to earth guy. Class can be dry at times. Tends to rush in presenting things on AutoCAD. Wish he would slow down so I can take notes on how to do certain things. Class is passable, you can show up and basically wing it. Homework is 30%. Drawing Assignmetns 60% and the final exam is 10%.

Get ready to learn nothing and struggle a lot. The projects instructions are so obscure, expect to get marked down for his inability to write good documents. He just reads from his written book in class. I think you should stay away from prof that writes their own book. They think they are hot stuff or something but they only read from this book.
One of the harder classes I have taken, but it was super rewarding. This class easily was one of the most homework intensive ones I took.

This guy barely teaches at all. All he does in class is "Read the book, chapter xxx and the reader, chapter xxx." He even combines two sections of class into one big class with more than 100 students. Worst professor ever.

The class was an awful experience. His lectures consists of him reading word for word from his laptop which is displayed on the projector. The last few projects (labeled milestones), contained such little information on how to implement the code that it took many hours of using ctrl-f in his 300 page course reader to even get an idea.

Absolutely horrible. His projects make no sense & take hours, & he barely gives you a week to do each project. For exams theres a study guide of 70 questions but he doesn't provide any answers so you have to figure everything out on your own. He gives no partial credit on assignments/exams. Harsh grading & all he does is read off his computer.

Assignments are time consuming and demanding, especially the later ones, but definitely hold value. His lectures are a bit of a pain; he goes through his reader on the projector, summing it up as he goes, which is worse than just reading it yourself. He is passionate about what he does though (teaching and his OpenMRS work). He is super kind.
Nice guy!
He's a knowledgeable teacher, but old fashioned and old schoolstyled.

I don't think Prof Levine is as bad as people make him out to be. His projects were long and tedious but you definitely learn a lot from them. Levine also gives good advice on CS career related things. His main downside is he can be a brutal grader on the exam and gives little hints as to what will be on them. Exams are like 60% of your grade too.

Definitely has to be the worst experience I've ever had with a teacher. Contradictory assignment guidelines, extremely harsh on grading, material presented extremely unprofessional. Slides and code are all word format, no syntax highlighting (as is the reader). Makes attendance mandatory but goes on tangents constantly. Go for another teacher!

Barry is literally the worst teacher at SFSU. If you need a class and he's teaching it, DON'T TAKE IT. Trust me, you'll be putting yourself through unneeded torture. He constantly talks about himself and how great he is. After a half hour of that, he reads word-for-word from his useless reader. You will not learn anything from this class. Horrible.

Interesting class, but really hard . Recommendation for new student: BE prepare more to do work and work hard. Don't Panic. Finish works as soon as possible and Don't expect too much help. Read the reader as many as you can.Finally, Make sure your program run for the test case is only way to win. Good luck!

As many others here have said, he is probably the worst. There are tests, quizzes and more even more quizzes. Although i like him as a person, as a professor he is the a nightmare, and his grading is the absolute worst. Working programs will get C!

He is the most awful professor I ever met. He taught little stuff during the weekly twice zoom meeting, but let us watch videos and read textbook all by ourselves. When I tried to get help from slack, his simple answers didn't help at all.... I don't know what's the meaning of this course.
He hardly teach on this class. He let us watch the video lectures, all the slides are just read by him and really boring. I learned this course mostly by myself.

There are quizzes, 6 assignments and a group project, and a 2 part final. The homework assignments are very long and difficult, so don't wait until the last day to do it. Robert Bierman is a smart professor and he is very nice when you ask questions. The 415 class is hard because he assigns a lot of assignments and you have to know the C language because he won't teach it. You will probably spend 60+ percent of your time studying time for this class.

Woah, I never thought that I was really surprised that I learned a lot about from his assignments and fundamentals we need to learn about operating system. This is what I was looking for and after all these years I finally found that this is really essential important for computer science. Imagine working with low level is very knowledgeable.

Intimidating due to heavy workload and grading. If you think your assignment was perfect, you will lose lots points for little things, so try not to worry about being perfect. Skim the reading and work on assignments ASAP, build little projects to learn a subject. Use lots of printf() for bugs. Turn in your non perfect work and you'll pass.

Very heavy workload and lots of suffering. He is a tough grader with class average of D for most assignment. But if you do your work you can pass this class. Workload consists of weekly reading , additional lecture videos, quiz, & assignment. I would recommend learning c language , malloc, and using virtualbox before taking this class.

Amazing person and teacher with a good background in cybersecurity. He gives your insight into a lot of things that you would not normally learn. You must turn your assignments in on time, no excuses, quiz's are not difficult. There is a really cool semester long project that you work on with a group, make sure you get a good reliable group.
I suffered from his class but I did learn a lot as well. He also is a very caring and knowledgeable professor besides being a very tough grader.
He's a tough grader but his material is very useful. You will mostly find yourself struggling in his class, but if you show good work, you should be fine :)

Overall good professor. At first I thought he'd not grade anything till the end of there semester by looking at the other reviews, but he did grade everything on time and provided good feedback. The group projects are fun and he goes over the material very nicely. Take his class!

OS is a pretty dense subject, but Bierman knows his stuff. This is a very heavy class. He holds lectures, expects you to read from the textbook each week, and has videos and quizzes which basically go over the weekly reading. Definitely a tough class, but you will learn a lot Utilize him for the 6 assmts and final project with office hours or slack

This class is loaded with information and he records each lecture and does try to explain the assignments and material in depth. Often says assignments are easy (ofc it will be for him) so it's lowkey demoralizing. Like what others said, graded everything the day grades were due so we couldn't even improve on later assignments with his feedback.

Although he did grade very past due. The cloth itself could be very difficult, however, he gives lots of workplace hours and recorded lectures. Although he did grade very late. The material itself is very difficult, but he offers a lot of office hours and recorded lectures. He gave us a very nice curve to compensate for his very late grading. He responds quickly to emails, and overall he's a kind person.

415-OS class. Covers OS material, dense material. Group project-combo of learned material, milestone assignments lead to it. Prof. Biermans videos explaining material & quizzes are invaluable. Grading takes time to ensure you actually did the work & give valuable feedback. Truly knows how these things work on a Yoda-like level. He really is Yoda

317webdev class. Covers HTML, CSS, JS, PHP, Node js, Express, & database, all useful. Group project fusion of learned concepts, w/ milestones of covered material. Ingrains the material in your head. Prof. Bierman presents it w/ a breadth of knowledge in a mind-blowing way. Always learning something new. Hands down the best webdev class ever!

615 programming (mostly C) w/ hardware, using Ras Pi. Make the effort & Prof Bierman is willing to work with you. Office hours are available. Cares about students & wants them to succeed & is a trove of knowledge invaluable to realworld programming. Grading: fair & takes time to ensure you did the work rather than borrow a solution. Good class!

Professor Bierman definitely has a ton of Computer Science knowledge, but it was annoying how he'd flex his industry experience to students. Despite this abundance of knowledge, Bierman was not a role model to look up to. His approach to teaching demotivated me to pursue a future career in embedded systems/C programming as well.

OS is a heavy-material class, so I give him props for keeping lecture material organized every week. He's very passionate about the course. But, lots of reading, quizzes, hard assignments, and we haven't received grades the whole semester so there's no room to learn from your mistakes (he also grades hard). If you take him, don't procrastinate.
Terrible professor. Semester is about to be over in 2 weeks and we still haven't received our Assignment 2 grades which we submitted 3 months ago

He is a professor who is clearly compassionate about computer science topics, but fails to properly articulate them to people who are still currently learning. He's a bit lax with how quickly he grades assignments, leading you to basically have to guess what your grade could be. If he did more live-programming exercises I would prefer that

Doesn't teach anything. I wouldn't take him if I had the chance but unfortunately, he's the only option at SFSU. Don't expect that you will learn anything. He will be talking about things that are not related to the HW or exams. Also, he's boring btw!

If you are serious about CS and learning, Bierman is a great professor for you. If you just want an easy A, go elsewhere. This class isn't easy but he does his best to help you as long as you are motivated and take the class seriously. He expects you to work hard but you will get a lot out of it.

Others claimed grades were late because he had a surgery. But guess what? Surgeries are generally scheduled at least one month ahead and his surgery (atrial fibrillation) was not a medical emergency. Therefore, he could grade earlier but chose not to. Also, what is the meaning of feedback after semester is over? This is absolutely unacceptable.

Prof. Bierman is really nice and cares about his students. Once per week, he gives the class an hour of his time to help answer questions. He will look through your HW carefully and give constructive feedback. He grades hard, but he curves a lot. The reason why final grades were delayed was because he had surgery (he gave us extra points for that).

Does not teach programming in C at the OS level, yet students have to know C at the OS level. Does not answer emails nor Slack direct messages about project directions if your teammates become unresponsive on Slack. Does not start grading the first assignment until semester is over. Still no grades by Grades Due by Faculty.

We had a chance to change to C/NC before December 18. Now its Jan 4th he still hasnt finished grading half of my homework. And homework was like 50% of our grade. How am I supposed to know what to do and improve myself if he doesnt grade anything
It took Professor Bierman nearly the entire semester to begin grading the assignments he gave, which left myself and my peers unclear on how to improve throughout the semester to earn a higher grade.

Assignments are already hard and he said on the first week that he's a "tough grader" so we can learn better. I don't see a point of being a "tough grader" if he hasn't graded a single assignment even after 2 weeks from finals. Very knowledge and has a clear passion for the subject. The course had 6 programming assignments and 1 group project with weekly quizzes on iLearn. The assignments were challenging but still fun. The assignments havent been graded yet, but he stated that was due to the pandemic related shortage of graders and staff.

The final is due in two days and I don't know my grade for any of the homework programming assignments. Absolutely nothing has been graded in this class besides quizzes which are automatically graded by iLearn. He said he would grade everything during Thanksgiving break but "something came up". I will never take any classes he teaches ever again.

WELL organized and clear materials... Professor Bierman has everything in ilearn week by week, which is precious and hard for some teachers to do. BUT the worst thing is that he doesn't give any feedback or grades on assignments until the last day of the semester. So I still don't know what grade I get on assignment 1 :)

hasnt graded a single assignment from the entire semester yet. i havent gotten any meaningful feedback from any code ive written so i cant even tell if im doing well or poorly. when you ask questions, he gives horribly indirect answers that you practically have to decided to get anything meaningful out of him.

Clearly knows what he's talking about and has a good grasp on the topic, but lectures are just a constant flow of talking. Homework is done using C which you don't have to know coming into the course, but you have to look up most of it on your own. Finishes grading anything by the end of the semester the textbook is only used in the first half.

He is a tough grader but with good reason. He wants you to learn! He's not just trying to make it easy for you so you can join the tech industry. He wants you to have a clear understanding and a leg up on the competition. He cares that you understand the material and not just cheat your way to a good grade!

Professor Bierman is the greatest lecturer I have ever had! Even during this pandemic, I felt immersed in his lecture and learned a lot from it. He cares about his students and does everything he can to ensure we pass his class. But most importantly, he wants us to leave his class with a good knowledge of how the operating system works! THANK YOU

His assignments are extremely difficult and are written in C. He's a tough grader and has high expectations and does explain in topics in depth. Take him if you want to be challenged! Challenge Accepted! Time to Duel! Pikachu! I was panicking when I got a D, but in the end he curved us and I went from a D to a B! What a great teacher to curve us!

His assignments are very difficult and he grades hard on assignments. Make sure you come to class everyday and take notes of his lecture because this is a very difficult course. He is a really good teacher, willing to help you learn and succeed, but C programming language is just difficult in general. Take him and you will pass for sure, just try!

Professor Bierman is a nice guy that knows a lot about what he teaches. His lectures cover a lot of theory and it is often up to you to implement that into your code for the assignments. There's very little hand-holding in his class but if you need help he has plenty of office hours and was always very helpful when I attended them.

Intro to web dev class is too hard for intro class. DOES NOT give any feedback or grade assignments until last day of sem. You won't know how you're doing until last day. Don't take.

Hardest CS professor I've ever taken, and I'm in my last year. Doesn't grade assignments til the end of the semester. You can put in several hours of work on an assignment but still end up with an F. Save yourself and pick any other professor if you can.

Robert Bierman is the worst professor I've encountered at SFSU. He's knowledgeable about the material, but is unyielding in his work load. He has a curriculum he WILL hit, disregarding the class' inability to keep up. He's sarcastic and dismissive to legitimate concerns, all while failing to provide feedback to students. DON'T TAKE!

The worst experience I've ever had with a college professor. Had attitude and was never willing to actually help when I had questions - would answer briefly and sarcastically. The one time I emailed him for help, I was criticized for my question and redirected to the school website without any actual help.

Professor Bierman is very knowledgeable and experienced teacher. This course itself is not an easy one because it deals mainly with Operating system and the course is tough if you have not programmed in C, not C++. His Quizzes are hard, assignments are tough within short time frame, and majority of the class have failing grade. Avoid if possible.

He is one of the hardest CS teachers. If you just finish CSC340 and thinking to take this class don't do it. He gives very hard assignments and expect you to finish it in very limit if time. if you have another option go for that. Avoid him at any cost!!! or you will regret and it would be too late.

Dr. Kohls is an amazing professor who is very passionate about what he is teaching, so much so it rubs off on you. I took his class English 425 Language in context and the student lead work was wonderful for different perspectives. He always is able to produce a point in addition to whatever is brought to the class by the different students.

Prof. Kohls is a real gem in the comp department. Eng 700 is mostly student-led (students facilitate/present on weekly readings), which is great practice and livens up the class. Readings are all well-selected & stimulating (jigsaw format). Presentation on a composition scholar of your choice and a research paper (lit. review) is included. Take it!

It was her first time teaching and she mainly went off slides. You can tell she is passionate about teaching, just needs more experience. Luckily, shes open to feedback. She mainly grades based on quizzes, test and homework, but if you attend lectures even when not mandatory they aren't that bad. Attending office hours help too.

Grade is mostly based on midterms and in-class assignments. Midterms are similar to study guides and you just gotta show up and try the in-class activities. She's new and was willing to change how the class works based on student feedback. Very lenient in grading homework and final project.
She did not even bother to make her own slides!! Used some other Professor's slides.
Dr. Doolani is a new professor but is fair in her teaching and grading.
Not my first choice.

New professor looking to improve from active feedback, so don't be shy to reach out to her. Strict deadlines but very forgiving grading. If you don't complete all the code don't worry too much about it, turn in what you have even if its a error output. In-class assignments and tests carry the grade.

All material is from a powerpoint the pervious 220 teacher left. She didn't answer questions very well. Dropped my grade by 10% a week after finals were done and didnt respond to messages when questioned why.

I was really underwhelmed by this professor. She seemed to lack a solid understanding of AI concepts, which made the class frustrating. It might just be me, but I'd recommend avoiding this professor if possible.

People came to class expecting to learn ChatGPT, but it wasn't that kind of AI class! At first, I was surprised, but I learned a lot. The topics were basic, yet eye-opening. Our teacher was right AI is huge! One class can't go deep into everything, but it gave me a solid start and inspired me to learn more. Expect to spend time to study.
Is she for real? Super weird lectures
Take this class as a last resort.

Very good teacher. Wants her students to succeed. Always open to help. Exams are very easy as long as you study the "practice exam" and material (they are very similar). Assignments are a little hard, make sure to have a good partner/friend. The way she grades is very lenient, will give a lot of partial credit as long as you attempt and try!
Avoid avoid like mold on fry wall

She might has lack of teaching experience but she does her best to let student understand. The most challenge and not a beginner friendly is using C++, if you don't know the language the class will be very challenge. Take two highest exam to grade, so the final is optional. Has extra credit in HWs. Overall, her class is not that hard and challenge.

I thought this was the worst class in the department after taking 415 with Bierman. She is not bad after all. 5 Homework, 0 extra credit, she only gave us extra credit because 80% of the class had f's, extra credit did not even contribute to the final grade, she chooses when she wants to add it and when not.

She's a great lecturer, and the TAs are patient and helpful. The assignments are kind of challenge so I reached out to TA for help, he helped me understand the assignments. I found many of them complaint but there's always a way you can solve it out, by asking or learning more. Anyway, if you want to learn coding, you can enroll in this course.

5 assignments in total, 3 requires groupwork, and instructions are vague with no rubrics to guide. You have to guess which topics she's gonna use in midterms, and you only allow one sided cheat sheet. EC points aren't guaranteed to be in final grade. Lecture slides are 80% useless unless u knew C++ beforehand. Her lack of experience is evident

What runs on your PC might not run on the graders'.

Not beginner friendly. You can tell she's trying but her lack of experience shows. If you ask questions she can't really answer them so you end up having to self study. Her instructions are unclear and grading takes at least a month minimum. Don't take unless you are experienced in C++, even then it's not worth it unless you have no other option.

Pretty good professor. There's in class assignments everyday so attendance is mandatory. Material is fast paced and difficult so be prepared for that. The assignments aren't too bad but take a while. You must have deep knowledge on every assignment you turn in so people that use chatgpt beware. You can drop an exam if you do well.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS Terrible lecturer, all her info comes right out of the textbook, attendance req'd. The projs (50% of your grade, 5 total) are unclear & insane, you can tell it's bad when our current proj has a potential FIFTY PERCENT extra credit. midterm avg is a 60%, proj avgs so far have been 60%, 70%. 2 midterms, final can replace 1 tho
Taught the class with live coding. Gave pop quizzes for extra credit. Participation matters

Took this class last semester, and outside the first few classes and test day, no one ever showed up to class. 6 homework assignments that aren't too difficult, and the midterm/final in person. only ended up with such a bad grade because of the 0 on the midterm i got for other reasons, but easy class nonetheless

I recently took CSC 510 with Professor Timothy Sun. The class structure includes 6 homeworks, with 2-3 weeks allotted to complete each one. The homeworks are graded by the TAs, and Professor Sun curves the grades at the end of semester. He provides practice midterm and final with solution. Also, actual exams are similar to practice exams.

I don't normally rate professors but professor Sun is an exception. Never have i thought i would enjoy learning and writing algorithms so much. He breaks everything down to school level concepts and starts building on. you only have 5 or 6 homework and two tests which are easy, if you don't miss classes. take advantage of the office hours, I DID.

Took him because Jose's class was full, never regrated it. very clear and helpful on Homework. Ensure that every student has support they need to succeed. 6 homework, 1 midterm,1 final. Always available in Discord, and very humble. And practice exam is best to succeed in exams. No cheat sheet allowed. I think he is the best professor for CSC510.

The way the course material was delivered often left me struggling to grasp the concepts, and the examples provided in lectures didn't effectively clarify the main ideas. I believe there's room for improvement in his teaching method and how he engages with students to enhance their learning experience.

VERY good at teaching CSC 510. Lectures aren't recorded but slides are uploaded and clear and concise to understand. Homework is easy to understand and follow, I just turned a lot of them in late unfortunately. Practice tests are similar to actual tests, and 1 page of cheat-sheet is allowed. Highly recommend if you're taking CSC 510.

Great professor, his lectures actually have coherence which is honestly rare for the CS department at SFSU. The material is difficult but I feel like Sun makes it easier with his teaching. Write notes on what he says, not as much on what he has on slides.

Timothy is a gentle professor on assignment, his explains ideas in algorithms clear and precisely. HWs are not that hard if you do study materials. This class should be harder, and you should learn more from this topic.
Amazing professor, very helpful, organized, lots of improvement opportunities. CSC 220 is a weeder class regardless of who you take. Just study and take advantage of the extra credit opportunities.

This professor is disorganized, with unclear lectures and inconsistent grading. Questions get vague or dismissive answers, and deadlines constantly change. There's little feedback or support, and they seem uninterested in teaching. If you need clarity or help, don't expect much. Avoid this class if possible.

The professor is very understanding and worked closely with students to get an idea of everyone's individual needs. She takes suggestions from students on creating extra credit, and offers good advice if you reach out! As for coursework, it's Java heavy, but doing the projects will help in solidifying programming skills. Definitely recommend!

Professor Chen is kind, supportive, and always open to feedback. She provides clear instructions for projects, offers extra credit opportunities, and publish all course materials on Canvas. If you have any concerns, don't hesitate to reach out, she will try to accommodate.

Tracy is a good professor. She is new to the school but loves the work she teaches. Seriously get to know your professors once class is over. She can provide amazing feedback on work and grades very leniently. Though be sure to communicate if you have issues. She also loves Dragon Ball SPARKING! Zero. A+
Not great. She is new to SF State. For older reviews see her RMP from kent state.

A really fantastic professor, and a man with a lot of integrity. He is very knowledgeable, yet also very down-to-earth. I get the idea that he has had a really full career, and is only at SFSU out of a genuine desire to help students find their footing in the CS world. An essential resource for the department. For 746, be prepared to write a lot.

746 was my favorite CS course! It covered key concepts in memory latency, CPU/GPU parallelism, and technical writing. Dr. Bethel's lectures were fast, clear, and insightful. Homeworks involved coding, analysis, and papers in latex (don't worry, you will get detailed guidelines). Great feedback, no exams, generous grading. ~8–10 hrs/week.
Dr. Bethel is an inspiration to students. His classes develop the skills it takes to succeed, both the hard knowledge and the soft skills, such as technical writing.

Great professor, makes lectures interesting and easy for students to take the class. Work comes in the form of working on a 3rd-party application called Perlmutter, which was pretty fun to use. All quizzes allowed cheat sheets so its clear he wanted to make the class to enrich students and not stress them out with a hard elective. Take this course!

One of the best professors I had at SFSU, this class got me an internship and opened many doors. One of the most interesting classes, Prof. Bethel helped a lot both during and outside of class, offering career guidance and general support. I developed an interest in computer architecture because of this class, which I initially found intimidating.

Prof. Bethel is a rare find at SFSU. His background in scientific computing gives him extensive knowledge in research and computer science. He is dedicated to passing on his knowledge and providing practical, hands-on experience. His passionate and engaging lectures make him an invaluable resource. Don't miss his classes!
The professor was ok, but if you are not interested in calculating caches, memory, runtime and so on, switch to another class.

This is a review for his CSC 647 Quantum Computing class. Material is difficult to grasp at first, but it's presented in a decently engaging way. Homework is "easy" if you go over the lectures. Professor will post job and internship opportunities for Quantum Computing. Definitely not easy, but still a great class. I highly recommend.

I highly recommend professor bethel. It started with 2 coding projects and ended with 3-4 analysis projects and for each analysis project there are 3-4 questions. Just do the homeworks and you will be pass with a good grade.

Professor is caring and easy going. Everyday he makes lectures interesting and comes in with a very friendly attitude. Often he ends class early and allows for questions and help. He says reading is required but I found that most points came from doing homework and reviewing lecture slides which translates into quizzes and exams.

Class consists of five homework assignments with 3 of them being based on coding. He's really accessible during office hours and after class and gives great helpful feedback. Overall, you can tell he really cares about his students and wants everyone to succeed. He offered an extra credit coding project that was worth a good bit as well.
Excellent professor who knows his stuff and has high expectations from students

Attendence is mandatory as he gives attendance quiz. There are 5 HW,1 truth table,1 logic, 3 coding hw + 1 extra credit. HW is on NERSC cori supercomputer. Class is focused on MIPS, logic gates, C++, GPU programming, cuda. There are 3 quizzes (no final) but the quiz is difficult as it is free response and he doesn't really mention what to study.

I attended CSC 746 High Performance Computing in 2021 fall as a graduate student in CS. It's a difficult class but he's very patient and very knowledgable on the area he taught. He gave a lot of feedback on assignments but was not a tough grader. He can tolerate on my mistakes in the first a few assignments and expect that we learn and improve.
Great lectures with lots of relevant information to the homework and the major in general. Extremely clear grading and comprehensive lectures. What more can you ask for out of a CS professor?

Course consisted of 3 coding projects (plus an extra credit one) and 3 quizzes. Bethel covers interesting and important topics (he's still in industry) and has comprehensive slides & lectures. Can't say enough good things about him. The class itself is tough but he goes above and beyond to help you as an individual succeed.

Mr. DeVault was really nice and if you asked for help he would give it, but he was not very clear at times and would claim he assigned things when he never did. He is not very organized. He's fun to listen to, but the fact that he was not very clear sometimes was not helpful

Very willing to help, easy class, overall great teacher, save for that he is very absent minded and over three months, he forgot everything from the key to the class, to the essay which he assigned. He also delayed much of the work till the last few weeks of the class, though that may have been because it was his first time on the quarter system.
He was very helpful and funny. The class and especially his office hours really helped my writing. I think he wore the same shirt for the whole semester.
He is a great professor! Young, funny, and passionate. I highly recommend to take DeVault for ENG 414.
Young and passionate. Really tried to help his students learn. I strongly recommend this teacher. Wish he would teach ENG 410 :-(
He is not helpful at all.

Took him for CSC 256 prior. Nice guy, gives decent feedback. Homework is few and far between, more on paying attention in class. Lectures slides don't have much, but lectures are recorded to help study. Quizzes and tests are very similar to previous semesters, so that helps. If you need a class to fill out an elective, consider this for a bit.

The content of this course is kind of dry but Dr.Hsu does his best to provide motivation. He is a very easy grader, if you pay attention to lecture and study for tests, you will do great. Most students that do poorly here either don't go to lecture or sit in the back and play on their phones. Homework is easy and practice tests are always provided.

This is not an intro class, take literally any other professor. He was insensitive and expected everyone to have background knowledge on computer programming before taking this intro class. Midterms and final were nothing like any assignments we ever did in class.

Very helpful and definitely would answer any questions you have. Projects got very hard halfway through the semester, but it's all based on lectures he gave so it's like a combo of everything you learned. Tests were pretty hard, but professor allows open notes for a part of it. You really need to take the time to code by yourself outside of class.

Nice person but class felt disorganized Lectures are long and it's personally hard to pay attention, and not paying attention means you fumble that assignment/quiz/midterm/final, which are all in-person Good feedback though and all material is similar to previous semesters, which he reviews, so pay attention for those

He's an overall good teacher he really wants you to learn and will even spend more time in class explaining projects. The projects are cumulative so if you want to pass pay attention from the beginning and make sure to understand concepts. Start on projects early, I barely knew how to code and did well so this should be a breeze for coders.

The content starts off easy and nice but will definitely get harder. I did every single assignment and project however the exams were way more difficult and he would mark off points by a lot for mistakes. Study the old exams given for practice and stay on top of your work, dont be scared to ask dumb questions. I asked a lot...

He has the worst personality of any professor I've ever had in my life. Nonchalantly and with seriousness, told a student to switch majors because they didn't understand a certain concept. Absolute nightmare to interact with. Suggestion: don't interact with him unless absolutely necessary, self-study your behind off and just focus on passing.

Although his exams are similar to ones from the past, they're still difficult and you'll have to work hard to pass. Nevertheless, previous exams are very helpful. He's a little hard to approach but very understanding at times. Holds review sessions and encourages you to go to office hours. MAKE TIME FOR THE LABS.
His test and quizzes are very similar to the practice test and quizzes he gives you. Easy B or A! Very nice guy and replies to emails quick! Take him if he teaches 256 again!!

His tests and quizzes are basically the same as the past quizzes, which he provides you. He's a fair grader. I didn't get to know him personally (the person below claims he'll fail you), but it's super easy to get a good grade if you practice the past tests. His lectures are really helpful, and it helps you understand if you participate.

I thought he was a decent teacher when I started given that he was the chair. He does not treat his students fairly. Be prepare for his impatience, arrogance, and discrimination. He will fail you if he does not like you personally.

Lectures are long; although he does ask questions it's not very engaging. Material is gone through very quickly with little time to take notes or process the gamut of information you're being fed. Would have liked to have more assignments/exercises to understand the material.
One of the best prof I've taken in SFSU. Material is easy, clear grading criteria, easy HWK assignments. take him 100%

As a Chair and a professor, he has done a wonderful job teaching concepts. He was very prompt by email and helped when we had issues without staring at something for too long. Very supportive and will help with any problems you have. I would say, try your best on everything and if you get stuck, he will help you. He has my respect. I recommend him

He does a good job presenting material, but the projects are very daunting and time consuming. Not for those who don't have deep interest in hardware like myself. The class started okay but became more daunting and stressful later on. Pro: Exams very similar to practice and he's prompt, polite & responsive by email. He can be awkward in person.

As a Chair of the Dept, very prompt by email if you need help or advice on anything. As a lecturer, not too bad as far as assignments, but if you need help, he will help if you did some research beforehand. Exams and quizzes are similar to the practice. Assignments are related to lectures and help. Downside - Can grade quite hard on assignments.
Cares for your education, Really supportive in person. Excellent Department Chair. Expects perfection in class.
